records.people: Juan Diego Mosquera Pesantes (Banco Central del Ecuador, delegate and member of the Monetary Board, 1981; director and board member of Produbanco since 2014)
records.move: from Citibank Quito founding manager and Banco del Azuay manager to delegate and member of the Monetary Board at the Banco Central del Ecuador (1981), then to the board of Produbanco (Banco de la Produccion S.A.) from 2014
records.summary: Produbanco's own curriculum vitae for its board member lists, among his posts, 'Banco Central del Ecuador. Delegado-Vocal de la Junta Monetaria' in 1981, and his service as director and board member of Banco de la Produccion S.A. Produbanco from 2014 onwards. The same CV lists earlier private-bank posts at Citibank Quito, Banco del Pichincha, Banco del Azuay, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and BAC Corp Securities.

records.people: Saleh Ahmed Keshlaf (Central Bank of Libya from 1985; Director of the Governor's Office 1999-2012 and again from 2024)
records.move: from Director of the Governor's Office at the Central Bank of Libya (1999-2012) to bank board seats: board member of Arab Italian Bank (UBAE) 2005-2012, member of the Libyan Foreign Bank Supervisory Committee 2007-2012, Deputy Chairman of the Libyan Financial Services Company 2009-2024 and supervisory committee member of Joumhourria Bank 2012-2022
records.summary: A&T Bank's own board biography gives a full dated career: he began at the Central Bank of Libya's Research Department in 1985, was Director of the Governor's Office there from 1999 to 2012, advised its research and statistics department 2012-2024, and was reappointed Director of the Governor's Office in 2024. Alongside this it lists board or supervisory seats at Arab Italian Bank (UBAE), the Libyan Foreign Bank, the Libyan Financial Services Company and Joumhourria Bank. The page states no ownership for any of those firms, and the Libyan Foreign Bank and Joumhourria Bank are state institutions, so the move is filed as a public-sector move and is not counted.

records.entity: National Bank of Serbia vaults, Belgrade
records.relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
records.detail: The NBS Annual Report 2024 section 'Structure and profitability of FX reserves' lists the components of FX reserves at 31 December 2024 as foreign securities (59.16%), FX funds in accounts abroad (22.04%), gold in NBS vaults (13.26%), foreign cash and SDRs. The whole 48.1-tonne gold holding is placed in the NBS's own vaults; no foreign custodian appears. Storage, not management.
records.source_title: National Bank of Serbia, Annual Report 2024
